q-82559.name: Question 1
q-82559.problem:
According to the Chinese remainder theorem, which of the following systems of congruences has a unique solution modulo $60?$ 

$$
\text{I.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡1 & (\text{mod}\,3) \\ x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,4) \\ x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}\,\text{II.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}\,\text{III.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}\,
$$
q-82559.worked_solution:
The Chinese remainder theorem states that if the natural numbers ${n}_{1},{n}_{2},…,{n}_{k}$ are pairwise coprime, meaning that $\text{gcd}({n}_{i},{n}_{j})=1$ whenever $i\ne j,$ then for any integers ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},…,{a}_{k}$ the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡{a}_{1} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{1}) \\ x≡{a}_{2} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{2}) \\ \,⋮ \\ x≡{a}_{k} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{k})\end{aligned}
$$

has a unique solution modulo ${n}_{1}{n}_{2}⋯{n}_{k}.$

Let's now inspect each of the given systems in turn.

- The theorem applies to system I. The numbers $3,$ $4,$ and $5$ are pairwise coprime natural numbers. Therefore, according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $3\cdot 4\cdot 5=60.$

- The theorem does *not* apply to system II since $6$ and $10$ are not coprime: 

$$
\text{gcd}(6,10)=2>1
$$

- The theorem applies to system III. The numbers $5$ and $12$ are pairwise coprime natural numbers. Therefore, according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $5\cdot 12=60.$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only."

q-82773.name: Question 6
q-82773.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡1 & (\text{mod}\,3) \\ x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,4)\end{aligned}
$$
q-82773.worked_solution:
Since $3$ and $4$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $3\cdot 4=12.$

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,3)\,⟹\,x=1+3t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,4) \\ 1+3t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,4) \\ 3t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,4)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $4$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $3\cdot 3≡1\,(\text{mod}\,4).$ So, we multiply both sides by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,4) \\ 3\cdot 3t & ≡6 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,4) \\ t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,4)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=2+4s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =1+3t \\  & =1+3(2+4s) \\  & =7+12s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡7\,(\text{mod}\,12)$ is the unique solution modulo $12,$ and $x=7$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.

q-82564.name: Question 8
q-82564.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$
q-82564.worked_solution:
Since $5$ and $12$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $5\cdot 12=60.$

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,5)\,⟹\,x=2+5t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ 2+5t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $12$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $5\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,12).$ So, we multiply both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5t & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5\cdot 5t & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12) \\ t & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=5+12s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2+5t \\  & =2+5(5+12s) \\  & =27+60s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡27\,(\text{mod}\,60)$ is the unique solution modulo $60,$ and $x=27$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.

Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below. {x≡1(mod2)x≡3(mod5)x≡5(mod7)

EXPLANATION

Since 2, 5, and 7 are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo 2⋅5⋅7=70.

We will solve the system in two steps.

Step 1. Find the common solution for the first and second congruences of the system.

From the first congruence, we get

x≡1(mod2)⟹x=1+2t,t∈Z.

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

x≡3(mod5)1+2t≡3(mod5)2t≡2(mod5)t≡1(mod5)

As a result, t=1+5s, where s∈Z. Substituting this into the expression for x, we get the common solution for the first and second congruences:

x=1+2t=1+2(1+5s)=3+10s

Step 2. Find the common solution of all three congruences.

Now, substituting the common solution of the first two congruences into the third congruence, we obtain the following:

x≡5(mod7)3+10s≡5(mod7)10s≡2(mod7)3s≡2(mod7)

Since 7 is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that 5⋅3≡1(mod7). So, we multiply both sides by 5:

3s≡2(mod7)5⋅3s≡10(mod7)s≡3(mod7)

As a result, s=3+7u, where u∈Z. Substituting this into the expression for the common solution of the first two congruences, we get

x=3+10s=3+10(3+7u)=33+70u.

Therefore, x≡33(mod70) is the unique solution modulo 70, and x=33 is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
